svg.title: The Heart of Node.js: The Event Loop
svg.desc: Auto-playing 48s step-by-step explainer of "The Heart of Node.js: The Event Loop" (from img_7.png). Each step is highlighted in turn with what happens, why it matters, missing concepts added in lime, and a Node.js code example. Hover to pause.
svg.text: The Heart of Node.js: The Event Loop
Events are emitted, the event loop picks them up, callbacks are called. Over and over.
Puts it on the call stack

g.text: The Heart of Node.js: The Event Loop
What: All application code inside callback functions (everything that is not top-level) runs
in the event loop. Node is built around callbacks.
Why: Event-driven architecture: a new HTTP request, an expired timer or a finished file read
each emit an event, and its callback runs.
Added: The call stack (the loop only runs a callback when it is empty), promises and
What: Things happen outside your code: a request arrives, a timer runs out, a file finishes
Added: A promise resolving (fetch, DB query, await) is also an event; its .then / await
What: The callback for each event is put in a queue. It does not interrupt whatever is
Added: The call stack holds the function running right now. A queued callback only runs when
the stack is empty, which is why setTimeout(fn, 0) is never "immediate".
↑ busy... waiting for an empty stack
// 'later' prints only after the loop finishes
What: The event loop takes the next ready callback and runs it on the single thread. One
callback at a time, start to finish.
Why: No two callbacks ever run at the same time, so you never need locks for your JS
const cb = nextReadyCallback(); // from the queues
What: Your callback runs. It may start more async work (a DB query, another timer), which
registers new callbacks, and the cycle continues.
Why: Keep callbacks short: while one runs, every other request waits.
Added: async/await is just nicer syntax for this: each await registers a callback and gives
the thread back to the loop.
// await = "register a callback, let others run"
What: Events are emitted → callbacks are queued → the event loop picks them up → callbacks
are called, until nothing is pending.
Added: Call stack vs queue, promises as events, async/await as callbacks.

svg.text: Callbacks run only when the stack is empty
→ it waits for the stack and the loop
Q: What is the event loop?
A: Runs queued callbacks on the single thread
